### Observed differences

- Four activities became near-mandatory. In the earlier window, A27, A36, A37 and A42 each appeared in only about 47–55 of 100 cases (roughly once when present); in the later window, each appears in 199–200 of 200 cases, about once per trace. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004]
- A25's successor changed completely: earlier, about 96 in 100 of A25's outgoing transitions went straight to A28, with the pair one step apart in 96 of 100 cases; in the later window A28 follows A25 only after four to five steps (99 in 100), and A25 instead leads to A36, A37 or A42 in roughly equal shares (about 31–34 in 100 each). [DIR001, LAG001]
- The A36/A37/A42 block now closes into A28 instead of A31: earlier, each of the three led to A31 in about 29–34 of 100 outgoing transitions and never to A28; in the later window each leads to A28 in about 31–34 of 100 and no longer to A31, while the three still follow one another in varying order. A28 now follows a block member within a few steps in about 199 of 200 cases, against 1–2 observations earlier. [DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009]
- A26's routing collapsed onto A27: earlier, A26 led to A27 in 54 of 100 outgoing transitions and to A36/A37/A42 in about 45 of 100 combined; in the later window about 98 in 100 go to A27, and an A26-then-block sequence within five steps nearly vanished (92 cases earlier, 1–2 in the later window). [DIR002, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006]
- The block moved earlier in the trace while A28, A26 and A27 moved later: mean relative position fell from about 0.59 to about 0.41 for A36, A37 and A42, and rose from about 0.40 to 0.46 for A28, 0.54 to 0.60 for A26 and 0.58 to 0.63 for A27. [POS004, POS006, POS007, POS008, POS002, POS003]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility of a structural rewiring around A25, A26 and the block A36/A37/A42, combined with these activities becoming mandatory. In the earlier window, A25 passed control directly to A28, A26 split its outgoing flow between A27 (about 54 in 100) and the A36/A37/A42 block (about 45 in 100), and the block — present in only about half of the cases — closed into A31. In the later window, A25 leads into the block (about one third each), the block closes into A28 rather than A31, A26 routes almost exclusively to A27, and A27 as well as the block occur in essentially every case; A31, no longer fed by the block, now consistently follows A26 by two steps (97 in 100) where the distance was previously mixed. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, LAG001, LAG003, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009]

This goes beyond what chance sampling typically produces: 26 control-flow items qualified against fewer than one expected for an unchanged process, every item's difference exceeds 199 of 200 random re-splits, and the evidence is direct (participation, successor and adjacency indicators) and mutually consistent. The new edges (A25 into the block, block into A28) were absent earlier and the old ones (A25 to A28, block to A31) essentially disappeared with about 200 observations per window, which sampling variation in a stable process does not plausibly explain. [DIR001, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, LAG001, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009]

Limitations: the evidence cannot rule out that the two windows sample a gradual shift in the mix of two coexisting process variants rather than a single rewiring, although near-universal participation afterwards (199–200 of 200, against about half before) makes a stable half-and-half mixture unlikely. The block's outgoing behaviour in the later window is observed only for A36, A37 and A42, so A27's exact placement after the change rests on its position and the A26 routing alone. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, DIR002, POS003]

Other differences: minor position drifts — A25 occurs slightly earlier (mean relative position about 0.37 to 0.35) and A31 slightly later (about 0.63 to 0.66) in the later window. [POS001, POS005]
